label: Cardiac excitation-contraction coupling

level_contributions.8: calcium release and reuptake by the sarcoplasmic reticulum via the T-tubule
level_contributions.9: channel gating, troponin binding, actin-myosin interaction
level_contributions.10: cross-bridge cycling rate and ATP consumption

state_variables.name: cytosolic calcium, diastolic
state_variables.note: predominantly isolated myocyte preparations; human in-vivo inferred

state_variables.name: developed tension
state_variables.note: preparation-dependent; no single human in-vivo figure is available and none is invented

mechanism: membrane depolarization arrives at the T-tubule
L-type calcium channels open, admitting a small calcium influx
ryanodine receptors on the sarcoplasmic reticulum activate
calcium-induced calcium release raises cytosolic calcium
tropomyosin shifts, exposing actin binding sites
ATP-dependent power stroke slides the filaments
SERCA returns calcium to the sarcoplasmic reticulum and the sodium-calcium exchanger extrudes the remainder
troponin releases calcium and cross-bridges detach

feedback_loops.description: Length-dependent activation (Frank-Starling): greater end-diastolic sarcomere length increases myofilament calcium sensitivity and developed tension
feedback_loops.damping: bounded by the descending limb of the length-tension curve above approximately 2.2 um, and by pericardial restraint at chamber level

failure_states.downstream: rigor; relaxation fails before contraction does

limitations: Quantitative parameters derive predominantly from animal and isolated-preparation work; human in-vivo cytosolic calcium at this resolution does not exist. Cross-species transfer is flagged per INV-12. Transmural regional heterogeneity is real and is not represented. This specifies one exemplar cardiomyocyte, not a population.
provenance_source: A Map of the Human Body (seed corpus, ingested 2026-07-26); mechanism detail from primary literature
